evaluation_inputs.system_description: An Event framework where the application logic and framework are highly inter-dependent. The Main module is part of the framework, and the Event Manager interacts directly with application handlers. It features an Event Queue and a base Handler component extended by standard and application-specific handlers.

phase_1_discovery.initial_documentation_status: Fully developed architecture with class diagrams, component descriptions, and defined component interactions.
evaluator_inquiry_questions: Can the components of the architecture be reused for future projects?
Can the framework be expanded in the future to accommodate a new application or new components?
Will the system handle any input given by the user and handle invalid input?
Is the architecture consistent in behavior?
Can any new application-specific functionality be added to the architecture?
Can the system be modified in short time and cost-effective manner?
Does the architecture perform its event-processing task properly?

hardware_view_description: System accepts input via Command Line Interface (CLI)
Single processor execution implied (sequential event processing)
runtime_constraints: Events must be dispatched in a First-Come-First-Served (FIFO) pattern
System must maintain an 'idle wait' state until input is received
Application logic is embedded within framework components

quantitative_model_parameters.performance_proxy: Number of components involved in a transaction
quantitative_model_parameters.transaction_speed: Qualitative (Slow due to high number of components involved)

questions: Does the system allow unauthorized access?
Does the architecture portray data confidentiality?
Does the architecture process any task in the fastest possible speed?

architectural_approaches.approach_name: Event-driven framework with a central Event Manager and FIFO Event Queue
architectural_approaches.description: The supplied architecture centers event dispatch through a single Event Manager and a single Event Queue, with sequential event processing implied by the single-processor hardware view and FIFO runtime constraint. The main module is part of the framework, and application handlers are invoked directly by the Event Manager.

addressed_attributes.rationale: A single queue and sequential dispatch define the processing path, but the supplied model also states transaction speed is qualitatively slow due to a high number of components involved.
Centralized dispatch and a single event-processing path can make behavior more predictable, but the supplied inputs do not provide implementation evidence for fault recovery.
A central manager with defined component interactions and FIFO dispatch supports a uniform event-processing style.

architectural_approaches.approach_name: Framework-embedded application logic with base Handler extension model
architectural_approaches.description: Application logic is embedded within framework components, and a base Handler is extended by standard and application-specific handlers. This is the primary reuse/extension mechanism described in the inputs.

addressed_attributes.rationale: Adding functionality through handler extension and framework components suggests a direct mechanism for incorporating new application-specific behavior.
The shared base Handler and framework components indicate the possibility of reuse across projects, but the supplied inputs also say application logic is highly inter-dependent with the framework.
A common handler base can promote consistent behavior across handler types if the extensions follow the same contract.

architectural_approaches.approach_name: CLI-based idle-wait event intake with STOP termination
architectural_approaches.description: The system accepts input through a Command Line Interface, remains idle until input is received, and must support termination via a STOP handler.

addressed_attributes.rationale: A CLI input path and explicit handling for invalid input are the only evidence available for user-error handling; the actual validation strategy is not specified.
Idle-wait behavior and explicit STOP termination define operational control states, but no recovery or failover mechanism is described.

architectural_approaches.description: The architecture limits the system to one Event Manager and one Event Queue.

addressed_attributes.rationale: The limitation constrains concurrency and may contribute to the documented slow transaction speed; no evidence is provided that it improves performance.
A single control point can simplify interaction patterns and reduce variation in event routing.

scenarios.scenario_text: Given CLI input and a running event framework, when an unauthorized actor attempts access, the system prevents unauthorized access without exposing protected operations.

Given an event transaction in the single-processor CLI system, when multiple components are involved in dispatch and handling, the framework completes processing in FIFO order while minimizing component overhead.
Given a failure during event handling, when the failure is detected, the system immediately recovers and resumes event processing or transitions to a safe state.
Given invalid user input at the CLI, when the input is submitted, the system rejects or handles the error and remains in the idle-wait state until valid input or STOP is received.

Given a request for new functionality, when a developer extends the framework, the change is implemented quickly and cost-effectively by adding or modifying handlers without disrupting existing behavior.
Given a future project, when the framework is reused, major framework parts can be adopted with minimal adaptation while preserving consistent behavior.
Given a new application needs to be attached to the framework, when the integration is performed, the system supports the new application and can coordinate it with existing handlers.
Given a request to move from command-driven to window-based interaction, when the interface changes, the framework accommodates the new interface with limited architectural change.
Given normal operation with no input, when the system is idle, it remains waiting for input and terminates only when the STOP handler is invoked.
Given a need to deploy the implementation in another environment or programming language, when the implementation is ported, the framework remains reusable and adaptable.
